item.title: Bank of Valletta inaugurates renovated Ħal Qormi branch and investment centre
item.description: Bank of Valletta has inaugurated the renovation of its Ħal Qormi branch and investment centre, the largest in its network, which the bank said was transformed to give clients more space for private appointments and improved access to banking and investment services. All areas of the building are now accessible to everyone, with a separate entrance for an ATM area open 24 hours a day, and sustainability measures include rooftop solar panels, upgraded air conditioning, insulation and double glazing, with recycled materials used in parts of the interior. Figures based on an operating model put the project at a saving of about 76 tonnes of carbon dioxide emissions a year against the same building before the works.

item.title: Man awarded €17,000 after criminal case drags on for 17 years
item.description: The Constitutional Court has ordered the State to pay €17,000 to Clyde Zahra, who faced criminal charges for 17 years, ruling that his right to a hearing within a reasonable time had been breached. Zahra, 16 when charged in February 2006 with drug trafficking and involuntary homicide, was cleared by the Court of Magistrates in December 2013, but the Attorney Generals appeal then dragged on for a decade before the Court of Appeal upheld his acquittal in November 2023. Madam Justice Charmaine Galea found the delays were not justified by the complexity of the case, noted his defence caused only eight adjournments, and recorded a psychiatric certificate showing prolonged anxiety and emotional distress caused by the litigation. The court declared a violation of Article 6 of the European Convention on Human Rights and Article 39 of the Maltese Constitution.

item.title: Planning Authority approves eight-storey, 311-bed elderly home in Msida
item.description: The Planning Authority has approved an eight-storey, 158-room home for the elderly accommodating 311 residents in Msida, replacing the former four-storey facility on Triq Clarence and Triq Censu Farrugia that housed around 60 residents before being demolished in 2022. The 29m-high development by Care Rise Limited, designed by Edwin Mintoff, will include two underground levels, 83 parking spaces, a chapel, a heated indoor pool, treatment rooms and a 32-bed high-dependency unit, and is expected to employ 33 people. The additional height is justified under the 2017 Height Limitation Adjustment Policy for Retirement Homes, while environmental NGO Din l-Art Ħelwa objected that the buildings imposing invasive volume and blank party walls would distort the skyline. The permit includes a condition requiring the site to remain a retirement home through a public deed.

item.title: Drainage works in Mellieħa uncover shaft linked to historic mine
item.description: Recent drainage works on the system in Triq Ġorġ Borg Olivier in Mellieħa uncovered a shaft over 27 metres deep, the height of a nine-storey building, which had been buried under the asphalt. The shaft is thought to have served as an access point to the historic Tal-Madonna mine, which carried water from an ancient spring beneath the Santwarju tal-Madonna towards the north-west, probably from before 1912 when water began to be channelled by gravity from Burnuħħala in Imġarr. The discovery confirms the mine extended to that point, taking its identified length beyond 500 metres, with two further shafts thought possible under Triq il-Kbira, and old mines in the area are said to prevent inspection and maintenance work, putting the site at risk.

item.title: San Pawl il-Baħar objects to plan to regularise unlicensed beach bar
item.description: The San Pawl il-Baħar Local Council has submitted a formal objection to the Planning Authority over application PA/06595/26, which seeks to sanction a beachside building at Perched Beach, Buġibba, being used as a bar although it was not built in accordance with its permit. The council argued that legalising the development would permit further exploitation of the coastline to the detriment of the public and the commercialisation of a public space kept for swimming, with added light and privacy intrusion, potential traffic increases and pressure on public and residential services. It asked the Planning Authority to refuse the permit, also citing the Environment and Resources Authoritys own concerns about the applications environmental impact.

item.title: First operations under general anaesthesia carried out at Paola Health Hub
item.description: Seven surgical procedures, including hernia repairs, were carried out under general anaesthesia at the Ċensu Moran Health Hub in Paola on Friday, the Health Ministry confirmed. Until now such operations were performed exclusively at Mater Dei Hospital, so the milestone marks a further expansion of the facility which began operating in July 2025 and already offers gynaecology, orthopaedics, gastroenterology, physiotherapy, podiatry, respiratory medicine, speech and language pathology and manometry. Cataract and other ophthalmic procedures under local anaesthesia began in July, and endoscopy-related surgery is planned for the coming months once clinical and operational arrangements are finalised.

item.title: Metsola: Europe has the talent to lead in artificial intelligence
item.description: European Parliament President Roberta Metsola rejected the idea that Europe has already lost the global artificial intelligence race, saying the Union has world-class talent, technological expertise and industrial experience to lead in the field. Speaking at the informal European Council in Dublin, she said what is needed now is financing so that ideas can grow and succeed, calling for better access to capital, more opportunities for innovation to scale and lower energy prices, linked to negotiations on the EUs 2028-2034 long-term budget. On Ukraine she said Europes commitment must be matched by predictable and sustainable financing: This is not about charity for Ukraine, its about reinforcing and reassuring Europes security.

item.title: Urgent appeal for O positive blood donations after spate of incidents
item.description: Reserves of O Positive blood have fallen to critically low levels after a number of incidents, with an urgent appeal for eligible donors to give blood on Friday, 13 November. Health officials said lives are at risk because of the shortage, and the Blood Donation Centre in Gwardamanġa will remain open until 6pm, with donors asked to bring their identity card. A free transport service to and from the centre can be arranged by calling 2206 6201.

item.title: Maltese students to strike on 20 November over budget and environment
item.description: Students in Malta will join an international youth strike at noon on 20 November at the University of Malta quadrangle in Msida, organised by the collective Youth Strike Malta. The collective says the protest will target the Budget 2027 measures it says disproportionately affect third-country nationals and foreign students, along with corruption, overdevelopment and overtourism, the use of Maltese maritime spaces and Maltese-flagged vessels in transporting resources to Israel, and issues at the University of Malta including its debts, growing use of artificial intelligence and the quality of education. Organisers Nic Ellul and Johanka Nefe said the demonstration would also carry an international manifesto calling for greater investment in public services, climate justice and action against authoritarianism and far-right ideologies.

item.title: Nine mediators join the Family Court roster
item.description: Nine Family Court mediators have been appointed to help the court handle more mediation requests, reduce waiting times and meet legal deadlines, Justice Minister Clifton Grima said on Friday as he handed out warrants to the new mediators. Grima called on lawyers, social workers and other family-law professionals to keep promoting mediation as the best way to resolve family conflicts, adding that childrens interests should remain at the centre of proceedings.

item.title: Boy, 15, released on bail after nearly six months in isolation
item.description: A 15-year-old boy has been released on bail after nearly six months in isolation, following a case heard in camera with a publication ban on its details. The teenager was arrested at school and charged with several offences; his parents, who are Italian nationals, said he was first held in Division 6 of the Corradino Correctional Facility and later transferred to the CORS youth facility, where he was confined for 22 hours a day under constant surveillance. Magistrate Tanya Sammut refused a bail application on 21 October, but the Criminal Court, presided over by Judge Neville Camilleri, granted bail against a €7,000 deposit and a €20,000 personal guarantee, with a weekly bail-book signature and a curfew.

item.title: Abela tells EU summit: affordable energy exists nowhere but in Malta
item.description: Prime Minister Robert Abela told the European Political Community summit in Dublin that affordable energy is unavailable anywhere except Malta, where the government will continue to guarantee stable energy prices through subsidies on electricity and fuel. He said strengthening energy security must go hand in hand with affordability, as prices remain a concern for families and businesses, and that oil prices had begun to show signs of stabilisation, though it was "still too early for optimism". He pointed to the second interconnector between Sicily and Malta and exploratory plans to import renewable energy from North Africa as a "glimmer of hope", adding that whatever happens, the government's promise remains to keep prices stable.

item.title: Non-EU students face tenfold rise in residence permit fees under Budget 2027
item.description: Non-EU students coming to Malta will face sharply higher visa and residence permit fees under Budget 2027, with Bill 15 tabled in parliament proposing that long-stay study visa fees rise from €100 to €300 for standard applications and from €150 to €400 under extended service. The bill would also increase the initial study residence permit fee tenfold, from €50 to €500, and add an annual €400 infrastructure contribution. The Federation of English Language Teaching Organisations Malta has appealed to the government to reconsider the increases and consult the education sector first, warning they could make Malta less attractive as a study destination.

item.title: PN: government 'does not even listen to its own people' over Budget consultation
item.description: The Nationalist Party accused the government of failing to consult social partners before introducing measures in the coming Budget, saying it "does not even listen to its own people, let alone anyone else". Shadow Minister Bernard Grech and PN spokesperson George Vital Zammit said the Budget showed a lack of communication with stakeholders on issues affecting daily life, particularly population growth and its impact on traffic, healthcare and public services. Both said social partners had confirmed they were not consulted before the measures were announced.

item.title: MFA recovers part of €16,000 missing from Match Day Operations Department
item.description: A substantial part of the €16,000 that went missing from the Malta Football Association's Match Day Operations Department last October has been recovered after an envelope containing money was left with a parish priest, MFA chairperson Bjorn Vassallo said in a TVM interview. The association gave everyone with access to the safe the option to return the money at a particular parish church, and Vassallo said an individual was suspended in 2025 after an internal review identified a discrepancy of about €16,000. A police report was filed over the disappearance and police investigations remain ongoing.

item.title: Comino to become protected zone for Maltese honeybee breeding
item.description: Comino is to become a protected area for breeding Malta's native honeybee, with the Maltese Honey Bee Conservation Area Regulations due to be published on Friday. The regulations control the keeping, breeding and movement of colonies on the island to safeguard the genetic integrity of Apis mellifera ruttneri and reduce the risks of crossbreeding, genetic introgression and the transmission of disease. Colonies may be kept permanently in the zone only with written authorisation from the agriculture director, backed by a new registration, monitoring and inspection system.

item.title: Żejtun Labour committee opposes three developments in sensitive areas
item.description: The Żejtun Labour Party local committee said it opposes three proposed developments on land outside the development zone, in urban conservation areas or close to scheduled buildings, invoking the party's core values on protecting the environment, culture and national heritage. In a statement on Thursday, the committee said the projects would affect residents' quality of life and the unique character of the locality, and would add traffic and congestion to parts of Żejtun. The position was framed as based on Principle 6 of Chapter 2 of the party's statute.

item.title: CrediaBank posts record nine-month profit ahead of HSBC Malta acquisition
item.description: CrediaBank reported its strongest nine-month financial performance to date, with recurring operating profit of €87.3 million and net credit expansion of more than €1.5 billion in the first nine months of 2026, as it prepares for its acquisition of HSBC Malta. Loan disbursements reached €3.5 billion, 44 per cent higher than a year earlier, with third-quarter disbursements of €1.46 billion up 78 per cent year on year. Recurring net profit rose 56 per cent to €49.5 million and reported net profit of €37.4 million was 278 per cent above the previous year, with the bank exceeding its full-year credit expansion target nine months early.

item.title: Malta airport revenue up 15% as passenger traffic grows
item.description: Malta International Airport's profits topped €50 million over the first three quarters of the year as revenue increased 15 per cent to €136.5 million, in line with passenger traffic growth. More than 8.7 million passengers passed through the airport between January and September, with monthly volumes exceeding one million throughout the second and third quarters. Staffing costs rose just under six per cent and other operating expenses just under 11 per cent, while capital expenditure stood at around €50 million, including continued work on the new office and hotel development.

item.title: Borg: Malta can become a launchpad for medical innovation
item.description: Deputy Prime Minister and Health Minister Ian Borg said Malta has the potential to become a launchpad for medical innovation, speaking at the opening of MedTech World Europe in Valletta. He said the health ministry is exploring a more structured research, development and innovation programme in digital health, and that closer collaboration between government, healthcare professionals, academics and industry would yield innovative services for patients. Borg added that Malta's small size, bringing decision-makers and the medical industry close together, is an advantage in identifying challenges and finding solutions.

item.title: More than 200 children in Malta living in foster care
item.description: Some 217 children and young people in Malta are living with foster families, with the authorities continuing to appeal for more people willing to offer a home and a safe environment to children who cannot remain with their birth families. Of those in care, 118 are in permanent alternative care arrangements, while 25 people who have reached 18 still live with their foster carers. The figures were presented by Social Policy and Family Minister Michael Falzon at a conference organised by the Foundation for Social Welfare Services.

item.title: Birżebbuġa council petitions Parliament over persistent Ħal Far fish-processing odours
item.description: The Birżebbuġa Local Council has launched a petition asking Parliament to take concrete action on the persistent odour in the area associated with fish processing at the Ħal Far industrial zone. The council said the problem, reported since 2022, continues to affect the quality of life of residents and neighbouring communities despite repeated complaints, reports and interventions, with no permanent solution yet found. The petition, which residents can sign at the council offices, asks that the issue be referred to the House of Representatives for parliamentary scrutiny.

item.title: Former Chief Justice De Gaetano: jury system needs reform, not abolition
item.description: Former Chief Justice Vincent De Gaetano said Malta's jury system should be retained but changed, calling for more transparency and closer attention to how jurors are selected. Speaking on the Attwalità programme about the verdicts in the Yorgen Fenech and Lorin Scicluna cases and the commentary that followed, he said the system needs to remain but must be reformed. He also noted it is normal for juries to reach the wrong verdict in some cases, and that the number of cases reaching trial must be taken into account.

item.title: Msida Public Library moves into primary school, serving 500 pupils and residents
item.description: The Msida Public Library has relocated to larger premises inside Msida Primary School, creating a space for reading, studying and educational activities for the school's roughly 500 pupils, their families and the wider community. The library previously operated from the Msida Local Council building, and an agreement with the school administration allowed it to move into a room already designed for library use. It was inaugurated by Education Minister Byron Camilleri and Local Government Minister Alison Zerafa Civelli with Msida Mayor Charles Selvaggi.

item.title: Maltese creators denied Meta monetising tools, MEP Agius takes issue
item.description: Maltese content creators remain locked out of money-making features on Facebook and Instagram that are available to their counterparts in other EU member states, MEP Peter Agius told the European Parliament in Brussels. A group of Maltese creators met Agius to raise the issue, which centres on monetisation tools such as In-stream Ads, Subscriptions and Stars. Despite reportedly meeting the other eligibility requirements, Maltese creators remain excluded from certain of these programmes, and Agius has taken the matter up with Meta.

item.title: MEP Peter Agius wins libel case over EU-funded 'sheep farm' allegations
item.description: Magistrate Joseph Gatt dismissed on Friday a libel claim brought against MEP Peter Agius by developer Kurt Buhagiar, who had sued over statements questioning whether more than €350,000 in EU agricultural funds had been used to build a villa rather than a sheep farm in Għajn Riħana. Buhagiar, one of the developers linked to the Corradino building collapse that claimed the life of Jean Paul Sofia, failed to prove Agius's statements caused or were likely to cause serious harm to his reputation. The court weighed the public interest in the allocation of EU funds against freedom of expression in political debate.

item.title: Budget Barometer: 44% want less dependence on foreign workers but no worse services
item.description: A survey of 400 Maltese citizens published in the fourth Budget Barometer 2027 found that 44% want Malta to depend less on workers from outside the EU, but most of them are unwilling to accept the trade-offs. Asked first about services, large majorities rejected fewer or longer waits in care homes for elderly relatives (87%), less frequent buses or cancelled routes (86%) and delays and higher costs in building and renovating (80%). Among those backing the reduction, 73% said longer hospital waiting times for non-urgent appointments were not acceptable, 84% rejected fewer places in elderly homes, and 82% rejected a less frequent or cancelled bus service. Seventy per cent consider the Budgets new fees and restrictions on third-country nationals necessary, and 18% said traffic and transport was what the Budget left out.

item.title: MEP Peter Agius wins libel case over EU-funded sheep farm allegations
item.description: Magistrate Joseph Gatt dismissed on Friday a libel claim brought against MEP Peter Agius by developer Kurt Buhagiar, who had sued over statements questioning whether more than €350,000 in EU agricultural funds had been used to build a villa rather than a sheep farm in Għajn Riħana. Buhagiar, one of the developers linked to the Corradino building collapse that claimed the life of Jean Paul Sofia, failed to prove Agiuss statements caused or were likely to cause serious harm to his reputation. The court weighed the public interest in the allocation of EU funds against freedom of expression in political debate.

item.title: NSO: 79 new vehicles licensed daily, total reaches 468,367
item.description: An average of 79 motor vehicles were newly licensed every day in Malta during the third quarter of 2026, with 7,235 vehicles licensed between July and September, according to National Statistics Office figures. The stock of licensed vehicles rose by 4,633 to 468,367 by the end of September, a net average growth of around 50 vehicles a day, with passenger cars accounting for 72.9% of the total. Electric and plug-in hybrid vehicles together make up 25,220 vehicles, or 5.4% of the fleet, with fully electric registrations up 6.4% on the previous quarter; petrol vehicles still dominate at 57.9% and diesel at 33.2%.

item.title: Heritage Malta reopens Fort Delimara for a two-day guided tour
item.description: Fort Delimara at Delimara Point will reopen on 21 and 22 November for guided tours of the former military site, Heritage Malta announced. The forts four 38-ton guns are the last surviving examples of their kind in the world still on their original carriages and platforms, in the chambers where they were installed. Restoration work has returned the 1876-84 fort to the layout it had when the British military left in 1964, with eight hourly tours each day from 9am to 5pm.

item.title: Man charged over alleged abuse of eight-year-old boy remanded in custody
item.description: A 24-year-old man was remanded in custody on Friday and pleaded not guilty to four charges over the alleged sexual abuse and harassment of a boy who is now eight. Sailesh Shrestha, a Nepalese national residing in St Pauls Bay, was accused of touching the child while watching cartoons at the boys fathers residence in Bormla when the child was seven. The mother reported the case to police on 25 September, the accused was arrested in a Naxxar supermarket on 11 November, and the court issued a protection order in favour of the minor.

item.title: Theatre director calls for culture minister's resignation over censorship concerns
item.description: Maltese theatre director Mario P. Azzopardi called for Culture Minister Malcolm Paul Agius Galea's resignation, arguing that growing distrust and concerns over censorship have made the position untenable. Azzopardi described the minister as "a good well meaning honest man", but said that honesty is what allows censorship to be justified through good intentions, and insisted the central issue is one of trust rather than competence. He acknowledged the minister's professional abilities but suggested they would be better suited to a medical role.

item.title: Court orders State to pay €135,067 over decades-old rent law
item.description: The First Hall of the Civil Court has ordered the State Advocate to pay €135,067 to Marsa property owner Joseph Gauci, finding that Maltas rent protection laws breached his fundamental right to the peaceful enjoyment of his property. Judge Abigail Lofaro awarded €134,567.32 in pecuniary damages plus €500 in non-pecuniary damages, with legal interest running from the date of the judgment, after a commercial property at 29, Timber Wharf leased under a protected tenancy since 1952 was inherited by Gauci.

item.title: Man grievously injured in Gozo traffic collision
item.description: A 26-year-old Brazilian man residing in San Lawrenz sustained grievous injuries in a traffic accident in Xewkija on Thursday evening, police said. The collision took place at around 9.10pm on Triq it-Tessuti between a TVS motorcycle driven by the Brazilian national and a Ford Transit van driven by a 37-year-old man living in Xagħra. The motorcyclist was given medical assistance at the scene and taken to Gozo General Hospital, where he was certified as seriously injured, with police investigations under way.

item.title: CrediaBank reports increased profit as it prepares to acquire HSBC Malta
item.description: Greek lender CrediaBank reported net profits of €37.4 million for the first nine months of the year, against about €9.9 million in the same period of 2024, a 278% increase, as it prepares to acquire HSBC Malta subject to regulatory approval. New loan disbursements reached €3.5 billion, up 44% year on year, while customer deposits stood at almost €8.8 billion and the cost-to-recurring-income ratio fell from 65.8% to 57.2%. The takeover is expected to push the group past €18 billion in total assets and give it a significant presence in Malta, where outgoing lender HSBC Malta recorded an adjusted pre-tax profit of €80 million in the first nine months of 2026.

item.title: Chamber of SMEs warns non-EU student fee hikes risk Malta's competitiveness
item.description: The Malta Chamber of SMEs said on Friday it was seriously concerned about proposed fee increases for non-EU students, warning that tenfold rises could undermine Malta's competitiveness as an international education destination. Students from outside the EU could face at least €1,200 in government fees when applying to study in Malta from next year under the Budget 2027 implementation Bill. The chamber said social partners were not consulted before the measures were announced.

item.title: Over 400 residents oppose industrial complex on ODZ farm in Ħal Farruġ
item.description: More than 400 residents in Ħal Farruġ, Luqa, have objected to plans to demolish a farm and replace it with industrial storage and distribution units, despite the Planning Authoritys case officer recommending approval. The roughly 14,000 square metre site opposite St Vincent de Paul, close to Wied il-Kbir, lies outside the development zone and within a valley system protected by several planning policies, and residents say the application describes the farm as disused despite continued farming. The proposal follows an earlier 2018 application for a warehouse and car park on the same plot.

item.title: Malta Enterprise received 200 INVEST applications worth €1.5 billion
item.description: Malta Enterprise received applications for 200 projects under its INVEST scheme this year, representing about €1.5 billion of investment in the Maltese economy, Economy Minister Silvio Schembri said during his ministrys Budget 2027 estimates. Schembri said the scheme has been extended for six months and pointed to a 10 percentage-point cut in the tax rate on reinvested profits and a €120 million scheme offering a 60% tax credit on eligible investments. He also set a national ambition for 40% of local businesses to be using artificial intelligence within five years.

item.title: Ex-MEA chief: ministers were warned of population growth crisis in 2017
item.description: Former Malta Employers Association chief Joseph Farrugia said ministers were warned as early as November 2017 that uncontrolled population growth could lead to Maltas implosion. Farrugia said he was invited to brief both the cabinet and Labour Party officials after the MEA published a position paper on the issue, calling for research into the impact on property and rental prices, regional density and the road, electricity and water networks. Finance Minister Clyde Caruana said a 2018 report he authored on the strain growth would put on housing, hospitals, schools and roads was shelved.

item.title: Lydia Abela's Gozo guesthouse could almost double to 40 beds
item.description: The prime minister's wife, Lydia Abela, has applied for planning permission to extend the couple's Xewkija guesthouse to 20 bedrooms, giving it a capacity of 40 guests. The number of bedrooms proposed has risen from eight in 2023 to 11 in 2025 and now 20, and the latest application also seeks to extend the basement excavation, move the pool to basement level and extend the left side of the property. The application has yet to be approved, and Robert Abela has previously faced questions over the financing of the guesthouse.

item.title: Global Microsoft outage hits Maltese government, schools and MaltaPost
item.description: A worldwide Microsoft failure affecting Outlook, Teams, OneDrive and SharePoint has disrupted government services in Malta, the Malta Information Technology Agency confirmed, with government emails delayed or intermittently unavailable. The impact spread visibly to MaltaPost, whose customer support systems failed and which directed callers to a phone line, Facebook and its Marsa desks, and to schools, where San Andrea School postponed an online parents day and Chiswick House asked parents to telephone rather than email. MITA stressed its managed systems and websites were not impacted and warned users to be vigilant against phishing attempts, while the Malta Union of Teachers said the effect on teaching was limited because most educators had a professional development day. Microsoft attributed the disruption to elevated load on its infrastructure, said it was not aware of any malicious activity, and later reported broader improvements in North America, sustained improvements across much of Europe as the outage, which hit 74 countries and territories, eased.

item.title: Non-EU partners of Maltese to face residence permit fee rise from €50 to €800
item.description: Budget 2027 documents raise the residence permit application fee for non-EU nationals who are partners of Maltese residents, and for third-country workers bringing a family member to Malta, from €50 to €800 as of 1 January 2027. The €750 increase was set out in a 270-page document tabled on Budget Day but was not mentioned in the budget speech itself. Civil society organisation Repubblika said the change could keep low-income foreign workers separated from their families for years and condemned the governments decision.
